absent: Bit positions and full composition of XFEATURE component masks referenced but not defined in this lane.
Lifecycle and writer of the static branch indicator for dynamic FPU state size.
Numeric outcomes of width selection and layout of register and descriptor structures referenced by FRED and GS loaders.
Base addresses, discovery and counter width handling for HPET and timer interrupt routing.
Model register numbers, feature flag encodings and fault behavior for FSGSBASE and LKGS paths.
Tracer infrastructure details including fentry placement, perf register layout and direct caller call chain.
Caller contracts for unterminated or invalid pointers in 32 bit string comparison.
Futex operation code values, user access scope semantics and exception type handling.
GART table entry format, PCI device setup and interaction with memory map beyond validation checks.
Vendor family model numeric encodings and source of CPU data for Geode checks.
Per CPU instance placement for interrupt statistics and trigger conditions for L1TF flush flag.
PKMAP base and last values, page shift, and TLB and lazy MMU helper contracts.
Breakpoint register programming and debug register interaction for length and type codes.

findings.text: Supervisor full set is the union of the supported supervisor set, the independent set and the unsupported supervisor set.
Persistent processor extended state mask is the union of the user restore set and the supported supervisor set.
Signal frame init optimization mask is the union of the tile set and the user dynamic set.
Predicate reports whether extended state size can vary at runtime. One build consults a static branch indicator while the alternate build always reports false. Both builds are always inline and pure.
Frame offset selects four on the narrower build and eight on the wider build through a width selector.
Two return encodings are defined, one for supervisor return and one for user return, each as a distinct four byte pattern.
Stack frame mask keeps an unsigned long aligned to sixty four bytes by clearing the low six bits.
Configuration word packs a redzone amount of one at bit six, an interrupt stack level at bit nine and an entry address held unshifted in an unsigned long.
Event info holds an event data word followed by a reserved word, both unsigned long, for values such as fault address or debug status.
FRED frame embeds register state followed by event info. Helpers obtain the info from a register pointer through container linkage and read its event data word.

Entry helper from virtualization builds a supervisor descriptor with kernel data segment, caller type and vector, nonmaskable flag derived from type equality and long mode set, then invokes low level entry.

Stack base synchronizer writes the supplied value to a per CPU slot when active. When inactive, synchronizer and exception and stack init plus setup completion are empty and event data fetch returns zero.
Four always inline helpers directly read and write FS and GS bases with dedicated instructions, with writes treated as clobbering memory.
CPU FS base access uses direct base instructions when the boot CPU advertises the FSGSBASE feature and otherwise uses the FS base model register.
Tracer call address equals the fentry symbol address, call size is five, maximum call offset equals endbranch size, and operations support is advertised as one.

Call adjustment returns its input unchanged. Symbol resolution steps back by one endbranch size when an endbranch precedes fentry, otherwise unchanged, with a generic alias exposing the resolver. One build of the endbranch test always reports false.

Register lookup returns null when saved code segment is zero meaning registers were not saved, else the saved block. Companion helpers set fixed flags with kernel code segment for partial state, copy instruction pointer stack pointer and code segment with cleared flags for perf, and update saved instruction pointer.
Traced return address is obtained by dereferencing the traced stack pointer as a pointer to unsigned long.
Graph function name is self aliased and its trampoline address equals the generic graph address.
Direct caller setup emulates a call by storing the destination in the saved origin field.
Dynamic tracer arch record carries no extra fields on this architecture.
Helper making tracer operations read only is an empty inline.
System call symbol matcher is advertised as present and compares names after skipping 64 bit, 32 bit, generic do and plain prefixes.
Thirty two bit string compare implements lexicographic unsigned byte comparison returning zero on equality and signed nonzero otherwise, with bounded form also stopping at the count limit.
Compat system call tracing is marked ignored, with compat detection delegating to the thirty two bit syscall predicate.

User futex updater runs under a scoped user access guard. It supports set by exchange, add by locked add, and or and-not and xor by locked compare exchange loops, returning not supported for other codes and bad address on fault. Compare exchange helper does a locked compare exchange under the same guard and returns observed value.
Futex user memory operations carry fault type exception entries that redirect a faulting access to a handler returning a bad address error rather than faulting the kernel.
Futex user updates rely on locked bus operations for atomic read modify write across CPUs, with no sleeping lock taken in the shown paths.
Robust unlock helper returns saved data register as user pointer when zero flag is set in saved flags, else null, exposed under a generic arch name.

Entry valid is one and coherent is two. Enable is bit zero, disable CPU bit four, disable IO bit five, disable walk probe bit six. Invalidate is bit zero and table error is bit one. PCI offsets are 0x90 for aperture control, 0x94 for base, 0x98 for table base and 0x9c for cache control.

When disabled, aperture and allowance report zero with disabled true and early check and option parsing and hole init are empty. Size programming writes an order derived control word without enabling translation. Enabling programs a page shifted table address then sets enable and walk probe while clearing CPU and IO disables.
Aperture validation rejects zero base, ranges crossing four gigabytes, ranges overlapping RAM, and sizes below minimum, logging each rejection.
Aperture moves from absent or invalid to sized without translation and then to translation enabled with table programmed and CPU and IO paths enabled, gated by validation.
Platform checks identify one variant by NSC vendor with family five model five and another by AMD vendor with family five model ten, with combined check true if either matches.

GS loader prefers a dedicated load encoding with a fault entry that zeroes the selector on fault when LKGS is enabled, otherwise uses the legacy loader. Early init installs the native loader into the paravirt hook when applicable on 64 bit, and public loader selects native path on 64 bit and segment path on 32 bit.
Legacy GS load runs with interrupts saved and restored around the load, while the LKGS path takes no interrupt protection in the shown code.

Interrupt statistics enumerate kinds for NMI, APIC timer, spurious, perf, work, retry, platform IPI, reschedule, call function, TLB, thermal, threshold, deferred, machine check exception and poll, hypervisor callback and timers, posted interrupts, guest perf, posted MSI, APIC error and misrouted, ending with a max sentinel with conditional members. Container is cacheline aligned with optional L1TF flag and counter array sized by the sentinel.

Counter increment is a per CPU increment indexed by the counter enum, with an arch marker defined. Perf increment maps to APIC perf when available else empty. CPU stat accessor and softirq pending reference are aliased to arch and generic symbols.
Helpers set, clear and read a per CPU L1TF flush byte when the mitigation combination is enabled, with an empty setter variant for other builds.

Persistent map index derives from address offset from base shifted by page shift and address derives from index shifted from base, with mask for last slot. Cache flush is empty. Post map flushes lazy MMU mode and post unmap invalidates one kernel TLB entry then flushes lazy mode.

Mapping spans 1024 bytes with ID at 0x0, period at 0x4, config at 0x10, status at 0x20 and counter at 0xf0. Per timer config compare and route use base plus stride forms with fixed offsets for timers zero to two. Identity revision, number and vendor masks with number shift eight and vendor shift sixteen plus 64 bit and legacy capability bits, enable and legacy config bits with legacy values two and eight, and level enable periodic and capability plus width route and front side bits with route shift nine are defined. Period bounds are 100000 and 100000000.
Timer enable and status report zero, register read reports zero, MSI setup is null, and RTC handler is a pointer taking interrupt number and cookie returning interrupt status.
Huge page support mirrors presence of the page size extension CPU feature.
Breakpoint record holds address and mask as unsigned long plus length and type as bytes.
Length codes are 0x40 for execute and one byte, 0x44 for two bytes, 0x4c for four bytes and 0x48 for eight bytes. Execute type is 0x80.
Each header defines a unique include guard macro to prevent multiple inclusion.
Thirty two bit compare helpers show no validation of pointer validity or termination, so callers must provide readable terminated inputs and correct bounds.
FRED support has active mode with per CPU stack sync and event data available and inactive mode where sync and init helpers are empty and event data is zero.
Base and segment access select dedicated instruction paths when respective CPU features are present and fall back to register or interrupt protected legacy paths otherwise.
